question: A team's answers are frequently wrong, and someone proposes moving everything to the deepest-reasoning tier to fix it. What is the greatest risk in doing that?
options: A) The deepest tier will take longer to respond, which will slow the team's daily work down considerably.
B) If the cause is a vague prompt or a stale document, they buy a more confident version of the error.
C) The team will grow used to the deepest tier and find lighter tiers unsatisfactory afterwards.
D) The deepest tier will refuse tasks it considers too simple, so routine work will stop being done.
correct_answers: B) If the cause is a vague prompt or a stale document, they buy a more confident version of the error.
explanations: Incorrect. Response speed is a real trade-off but a minor one next to continuing to act on wrong answers.
Correct. Reasoning depth cannot supply missing context or override an out-of-date source, so the wrong answers persist while the allowance is consumed faster.
Incorrect. Preference drift is speculative and is not the reason this move can fail.
Incorrect. No tier refuses work for being simple; that is not a behaviour a user encounters.
